newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan wants U.N. to set up office in Liberia.
newsitem.headline: Annan wants U.N. to set up office in Liberia.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Monday he would recommend establishing a U.N. office in Liberia to assist the civil-war-shattered country after a small U.N. observer force leaves in about six weeks.

In a written report to the Security Council, he said the principal objective of the U.N. Observer Mission in Liberia (UNOMIL) had been achieved with the establishment of a democratically elected government on Aug. 2.

A peace accord signed in Abuja, Nigeria, last August ended a multi-sided civil war that broke out in December 1989. More than 150,000 people were killed in the war, and the country's key mining and rubber industries were devastated. Former warlord Charles Taylor was elected president in elections held on July 19.
UNOMIL, now numbering only about 30 observers, has been working with a 10,000-member peacekeeping force called ECOMOG fielded by the Economic Community of West African States.

"Pending further consultations with the government of Liberia, it would be my intention to recommend the establishment of a peace-building support office to succeed UNOMIL after Sept. 30," Annan said.

"I am convinced that such a presence could greatly assist the new government in its efforts for reconciliation and reconstruction and contribute to promoting peace and stability in the region," he said.
Annan said he would provide details of the structure, staffing and functions of the proposed office before UNOMIL's mandate expired.
